title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Section 50 (p. 650 bis) opens a new chapter, 'Schematic envelopes of discrete groups'. The context is the Galois–Teichmüller programme: the next sections, listed in the table of contents on the neighbouring page, are 'Lie approximations of Galois–Teichmüller systems' and 'L- and TL-groups'. The aim is to attach to a discrete group (e.g. a Teichmüller / mapping class group) a group scheme over Spec(Z), its 'schematic envelope', in which distinguished elements (Dehn-twist-like generators) become unipotent or quasi-unipotent sections. This page fixes the vocabulary.

Setting: G is a group scheme locally of finite presentation over a base S. The important case will be S = Spec Z.

Definition 1 (unipotent section). A section g ∈ G(S) is unipotent if, for every geometric point s̄ with residue field k, the fibre value g_s̄ ∈ G_s̄(k̄) is unipotent. Grothendieck does not use the usual Jordan-decomposition notion here. He defines it as: there is a homomorphism of k̄-group schemes φ_s̄ : G_a → G_s̄ with φ_s̄(1) = g_s̄. That is, g_s̄ lies on a one-parameter additive subgroup, with g_s̄ the value at 1.

Definition 2 (quasi-unipotent). g is quasi-unipotent if for every s̄ some power g_s̄^n (n ≥ 1) is unipotent. In characteristic p > 0 this is equivalent to g_s̄ having finite order. Indeed φ(1)^p = φ(p) = φ(0) = 1, and conversely 1 = φ_trivial(1).

Claim: if S is quasi-compact, g is quasi-unipotent iff a single n works, i.e. g^n is unipotent for some n. This is a uniform bound obtained by constructibility and quasi-compactness.

A 'Théorème' is begun and struck out. It is replaced by the question/criterion: is g unipotent iff there exists a homomorphism φ : G_a,S → G over S itself with φ(1) = g? Sufficiency is trivial. The next page discusses necessity:
- Over a field of characteristic 0, φ is unique (φ(t) = exp(t·log g)). Hence fpqc descent applies and φ exists over S.
- In characteristic p, uniqueness fails because of non-trivial endomorphisms of G_a vanishing at 1 (e.g. x ↦ x^p − x). Descent therefore breaks down.
- He asks whether a canonical or unique choice exists, even over a field, and leaves this open ('questions assez intéressantes').
errors: The fibrewise definition 'g_s̄ = φ(1) for some homomorphism G_a → G_s̄' is strictly stronger than the usual notion of unipotent element in characteristic p. Every φ(1) has order dividing p, since G_a is killed by p. So e.g. a regular unipotent Jordan block of size n > p in GL_n(F_p), which has order p^2, is NOT 'unipotent' in Grothendieck's sense; it is only quasi-unipotent. Consequently an integral unipotent matrix such as a 3×3 Jordan block over Z fails to be 'unipotent' at p = 2. The page does not remark on this. It is not a logical error, but it is a deviation from standard terminology that any later use (e.g. for Dehn twists in higher-rank representations) would have to account for.

Even for elements of order p, existence of φ over k̄ is a non-trivial theorem: Testerman, and Seitz in good characteristic for reductive groups. It is not automatic for arbitrary group schemes, and the definition implicitly presupposes a good supply of such φ.
The claimed uniformity of n over quasi-compact S needs a constructibility argument (finite presentation) that is not given; it is plausible but not proved on the page.

ideas.what: Schematic (Z-group-scheme) envelope of a discrete group, e.g. Teichmüller groups, as part of Galois–Teichmüller theory
ideas.modern_name: Integral algebraic hull / relative or Malcev completion over Z; Zariski closure of discrete groups in group schemes over Spec Z
ideas.usually_credited_to: Malcev (unipotent completion); Deligne 1989 and Hain, Hain–Matsumoto (relative completion of mapping class groups, over Q)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to Lie-type/schematic approximations of Teichmüller tower; not in this form

ideas.what: Unipotent section of a group scheme defined fibrewise via existence of G_a → G_s̄ with φ(1) = g
ideas.modern_name: Elements lying in a one-parameter additive subgroup; 'exponentiation' / G_a-saturation of unipotent elements
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical in char 0 (exp/log); in char p: Testerman 1995, Seitz 2000, McNinch, Proud–Seitz–Testerman

ideas.what: Quasi-unipotent sections (some power unipotent on each fibre; equivalent to finite order in char p), with uniform exponent over quasi-compact base
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck/Deligne in the monodromy context (SGA 7); standard
ideas.where_published: SGA 7 (quasi-unipotent monodromy), in the different context of ℓ-adic monodromy

ideas.what: Question whether fibrewise unipotence implies existence of a global φ : G_a,S → G with φ(1) = g; descent works in char 0 by uniqueness of φ, but fails a priori in char p for lack of uniqueness (Artin–Schreier-type endomorphisms of G_a)
ideas.modern_name: Existence and uniqueness of 'good' / canonical A1- or G_a-subgroups through unipotent elements; Springer isomorphisms and exponentials over Z or Z_(p)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Seitz (good A1 subgroups, 2000), McNinch (optimal SL2 homomorphisms, exponentials 2003–05), Serre (Moursund lectures on order-p elements)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly poses, and leaves open, the question whether a section of a group scheme over a general base (notably Spec Z) that is fibrewise G_a-unipotent comes from a global homomorphism G_a,S → G. He identifies the char-p obstruction as non-uniqueness of φ and asks whether a canonical choice exists even over a field. Later work of Seitz and McNinch on 'good' or 'optimal' G_a/A1-subgroups gives uniqueness in good characteristic for reductive groups. The relative-over-Z, arbitrary-group-scheme version, aimed at schematic envelopes of Teichmüller groups, seems not to have been formulated in the literature.
missed.quote: Pour que g soit unipotente, il faut et il suffit qu'il existe un homom. φ : G_a → G tel que φ(1) = g
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral (over Z) versions of relative completion of mapping class groups, with Dehn twists as unipotent sections, are still underdeveloped. A good notion of unipotent section over Spec Z would be the needed input for an integral Galois–Teichmüller 'Lie approximation'.

missed.claim: The page implicitly links the char-p theory of exponentiating order-p unipotent elements (Seitz/Testerman/McNinch) with integral envelopes of discrete groups in anabelian/Galois–Teichmüller theory. The later literature treats these two topics separately.
missed.quote: Enveloppes schématiques de groupes discrets ... le cas important pour nous sera S = Spec(Z)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Could guide integral models of Hain–Matsumoto relative completions, where the reduction mod p of Dehn-twist images must be controlled.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly definitions. The noteworthy point is an early, explicit formulation (over a general base, aiming at Spec Z) of the existence/uniqueness problem for G_a-subgroups through unipotent elements in char p. That problem was later solved in the reductive case by Seitz/McNinch in a different setting, and here it serves the unpublished programme of integral schematic envelopes of Teichmüller groups.
transcription_corrections: The insertion '{+S plat sur Z[?]+}' is doubtful. The image reads roughly 'sur un schéma de base S (& le cas important pour nous sera S = Spec(Z))', with no visible 'plat sur Z'.
The subtitle read as '(Cas unibranche)' is very uncertain in the image; the scrawl could be another word. It should be flagged as unreadable rather than asserted.
'pour tout fibre géométrique' should read 'pour toute fibre géométrique'.
The struck-out passage reads approximately 'Théorème. Soit G loc. de présentation finie sur S, S quasi-compact. Si g est unipotente, p...'; the transcription is consistent with this.
